summary.intent: Execute (and then gap-close) all plans in roadmap phase 68.1 of the CipherBox project using GSD's wave-based parallel execution workflow, taking a client codebase from stubbed owned/shared write-chain integration to a working, verified web runtime, then diagnose and fix real-world bugs the user found while manually testing (nested folder creation, cold-navigation into subfolders, PDF-as-folder misrendering, dev-stack health).
summary.outcome: All 14 original plans plus a first wave of gap-closure plans (68.1-15,16,17,18,19,20,21) executed across 5+ waves with wave-level build/test gates; verification scored the phase at 2/5 success criteria with concrete surfaced gaps (GAP-1 AEAD decrypt failure, GAP-2 cold IPNS resolution/durability, SC#4 shared-browser kind-cache gaps, SHARE-WRITE-KEY, GAP-6 dead itemName backfill); gap-closure planning and a second gap-execution round fixed several of these (durable TEE republish enrollment, shared kind-cache wiring, D-05 stale-record toast direction-awareness) and the phase remains open pending a further gap wave and full e2e re-verification.

repo: CipherBox web app has no SdkContext bridge — file read/metadata resolution against IPNS must use web-native primitives (resolveIpnsRecord from ipns.service.ts + ctx-free fetchFromIpfs) rather than sdk-core's ctx-based helpers, and this actually preserves the ROT-07 anti-rollback floor better than sdk-core's raw resolver

SealedChildRef carries readKeySealed/generation needed to derive a child's own readKey via unsealChildReadKey — bare ipnsName strings are insufficient, so read/write chain APIs must take the full ref, not just the name

Live /shares and /shares/invites REST API grants an entire subtree via one ECIES wrap of the root readKey — there is no server-side per-child-key field, making the planned collectChildKeys/ChildKeyDto design architecturally dead (implemented as speced but has no live caller)

sdk-core's issueReadGrant/claimInvite (grant.ts) produce base64 payloads but live DTOs are hex-only — web code must call wrapKey/unwrapKey directly with hex encoding instead of routing through sdk-core grant primitives

Write-permission share/invite creation requires the parent folder's writeKey, which today lives only inside CipherBoxClient's private FolderState and is not threaded to any web UI layer (SHARE-WRITE-KEY gap) — there's also no backend upgrade-permission endpoint (would need revoke+recreate)

migration 1750000000000-ApiSchemaCutover dropped the shares table's plaintext item_name column entirely; share.service.ts hardcodes itemName: '', making the REQ-4 shouldBackfill() feature permanently false/dead code — reviving it would violate the zero-knowledge rule in CLAUDE.md (GAP-6, deliberately left as an unresolved decision rather than unilaterally fixed)

mock-ipns-routing (dev delegated-routing mock) keeps IPNS records in an in-memory Map that is wiped on every container restart; records survive restarts only if they also got a DB row via the API's publish-time cache — so a subfolder created without full TEE enrollment can become permanently unresolvable after any restart

createFolder previously published child records without encryptedIpnsPrivateKey/keyEpoch, so ipns_republish_schedule got zero rows for subfolders — in production this means every subfolder's IPNS record dies at the 48h TTL unless a later mutation republishes it (fixed in 68.1-16)

mock-ipns-routing's healthcheck (`wget localhost`) resolves to ::1 while the app binds IPv4-only, causing a permanently 'unhealthy' container status even when the service works fine — fix is to healthcheck 127.0.0.1 explicitly
The API listens on :3000; :3001 is the separate delegated-routing mock (DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL target for web-e2e) — probing :3001 for API health silently hits the wrong service

D-05 stale-record replay bug: the durable ROT-07 sequence floor is bumped pre-publish, one step ahead of the client's own subsequent publish, so a relay replay from immediately before that publish matches the floor exactly instead of falling below it, sailing through enforceResolved as a plain ReconcileStaleError that was retried uniformly regardless of direction — fix adds localSequence/networkSequence to the error and only retries when network is ahead of local

Folder-store id desync (UUID vs ipnsName) was the dominant root cause blocking nested-folder creation across most of the originally-17 failing e2e spec groups — fixed alongside createFolder retry-on-ReconcileStaleError wiring in 68.1-13

Kind cache (D-02, wired in 68.1-04/14) was populated but never consulted by FileListItem/ContextMenu in the owned browser (files rendered/treated as folders) nor by SharedFolderRow/SharedFileBrowser (isFolder hardcoded true) — two separate wiring gaps needing separate fix plans (68.1-13 for owned, 68.1-15 for shared)

decision-coverage gate for gsd-plan-phase requires the informational tag placed inside the bold ID group itself, e.g. `- **D-04 [informational]:**`, not appended after the closing bold — tag placement outside the bold group silently fails to register

code.finding: isFolder was hardcoded to true, ignoring the D-02 kind cache — fixed in 68.1-15 to `!isFileRef(item)`

All five stubbed shared-write handlers (rename/delete/update/move/batch-move) wired to SDK client's shared-folder methods in 68.1-10; move/update-fallback still fails closed because fetchShareKeys remains a pre-existing deferred stub

resolveFileIpnsPrivateKey added as a new public method (68.1-12) so the web layer can derive fileIpnsPrivateKey without independent access to the parent folder's writeKey; createFolder (68.1-16) now enrolls new subfolders in TEE republish (encryptedIpnsPrivateKey/keyEpoch) fail-closed before any addToIpfs side effect; ReconcileStaleError (68.1-21) gained localSequence/networkSequence fields for direction-aware retry
updateFileMetadata never actually zeroed fileIpnsPrivateKey despite doc comments claiming it did (T-47-01 latent bug) — fixed alongside 68.1-12's write-chain wiring
restoreFromBin hardened in 68.1-16 to warn (non-throwing) when a restored child's own IPNS record fails to resolve post-relink, rather than silently succeeding on a dead record

workflow: When a subagent's tool stream stalls mid-run, GSD's execute-phase fallback is to spot-check filesystem/git state, then SendMessage to resume the same agent with its full context rather than restarting fresh — this reliably recovered work in two separate incidents in this session

Background task completion notifications can be lost if the orchestrator's session gets evicted mid-wait (happened after the 208-spec e2e suite finished at 18:13 with no re-wake) — recovery requires manually checking process liveness/log files and resuming the agent with the verified results via SendMessage

Serial (describe.serial) Playwright specs abort at first failure, so a raw pass/fail tally overstates health — most failing spec groups die in setup code that creates nested content, leaving their real coverage unexecuted; a single upstream fix can flip a large share of failures at once

Running full test suites concurrently from parallel subagents starves RAM (per existing memory) — this session's wave gates instead centralize post-merge build/test gates in the orchestrator after each wave merges

gsd-tools' decision-coverage gate is picky about exact D-NN bullet/tag formatting; iterating against its parser source (grep for the informational-tag matching rule) was faster than guessing tag placement
